AUD 1-AUD 2 The Audio 1 and Audio 2 signals are game PCB output signals that are generated by custom audio chips B3 and C/D3 of the Optlon Switch input and Audio Output circuit. AUD 1 Is the inverse of AUD 2. These signals are applied to the Audio/Regulator Il PCB and ultimately drive speakers 1 and 2.

Output circuit is clocked by LATCH, R89 latches the data on DB2 to pin 2 of R9, Producing the BANK SEL signal. BANK SEL is exclusiveORed with the address bit A10 by gate 56 to produce input address bit A10 for Random-Access Memory N/P1. BLANK Blank is an active high-level signal generated by counter M3 in the Z Intensity and Blanking circuit and ORed with Z BLANK by gate MS of the R-G-B Output circuit. When high, BLANK turns off transistors Q6, Q8, and Q10, which kills the RED, GREEN, and BLUE output signals to the display.

BLUE Blue Is a game PCB output signal developed from the data on line DVYO. When the data bit on DVYO Is high and latch K10 of the R-G-B Output circult Is clocked by STATCLK, the data on DVYO is Inverted and latched to pin 11 of K10. If both BLANK and Z BLANK are low, this data bit Is again inverted by gate L10 to tum on Q10. Transistor Q10 generates the BLUE signal for the display.

DO-D7 Microprocessor Data Bus lines D0-D7 form a bi-directional data bus between the Microprocessor, the Read-Only Memory, and the Option Switch Input circuits.

DBO-DB7 Buffered Microprocessor Data Bus lines DBO-DB7 form a buffered bi-directional data bus between microprocessor data-bus buffer F2 and Vector Memory Data Buffer P8; Coln-Door and Control Panel Input circuit buffers L9, M9, and N9; High-Score Table latches K2 and J2; and High-Score Table buffer H2.

DIS DAT Disable Data Is an active_low-level signal generated by test equipment connected to the DIS DAT test point. DIS DAT Is ANDed with the ROM signal by gate E3 to produce the enable signal for buffer £2 of the Read-Only Memory circult. When enabled, buffer E2 passes data from the selected Read-Only Memory to the Microprocessor Data Bus.

DISRST Display Reset Is an active low-level signal software-generated by gate L6 of the Halt Flag circult. When either RESET or VGRST Is low, DISRST Is set low When low, DISRST clears State Machine latch P4, DAC Reference and Bipolar Current Sources latch E8, R-G-B Output latch K10, Vector Scaling latch D7, Z Intensity and Blanking latch E6 and counter M3. In addition, DIS Presets the HALT signal from latch L5 to the high level.

DVG@O-DVG7 Data bits on Vector-Generator Data Bus lines OVGO-DVG7 are software-generated by the selected Vector Read-Only Memory or Vector Random-Access Memory. If Vector Memory Data Buffer P8 Is enabled (BUFFEN Is low) and the R/WB line is low, the data on lines DVGO-DVG7 Is passed through P8 to the Buffered Microprocessor Data Bus to be read by the microprocessor. Otherwise, the data on DVGO-DVG7 Is sent to the Vector Data Shifters and to the Op Code and Intensity Latches. .

DVX3-DVX12, DVX12 Data bits on X-Axis Vector Data lines DVX3-DVX12 and DVX12 are software-generated by Vector Data Shifters A8, B8, C8, and by latch C8 of the Op Code and Intensity Latches circuit. DVX3- DVX11 and DVX12 are the input signals to digital-to-analog converter (DAC) A/B9 of the X-Axis Output circuit. The data carried on these lines represents the X-axis change from the current location of the display beam. If DVX12 is low, DAC A/B9 operates only in its

ATARI lower 512 positions, which means a negative direction of change ‘on the display. If DVX12 is high, DAC A/B9 operates only in its upper 512 positions for a positive direction of change on the display. In addition, DVX11 and DVX12 are exclusive-ORed by gate B6 of the Normalization Flag circult.

DVYO-DVY12, DVY12 Data bits on Y-Axis Vector Data lines DVYO-DVY12 and DVY12 are software-generated by Vector Data Shifters F8, H8, J8, and by latch D6 of the Op Code and Intensity Latches circuit. DVY3- DVY11 and DVY12 are the input signals for digital-to-analog converter (DAC) F9 of the Y-Axis Output circult. The data carried on these lines represents the Y-axis change from the current location of the display beam. If DVY12 is low, DAC F9 operates only in its lower 512 positions, which means a negative direction of change ‘on the display. If DVY12 Is high, DAC F9 operates only in its upper 512 positions for a positive direction of change on the display. In addition, DVYO-DVY7 are applied to latch E8 in the DAC Reference and Bipolar Current Sources circuit. These signals, together with VCTR and VCTR, set the X REF and Y REF voltage levels (via DAC D9). Lines DVYO-DVY2 carry data representing the eight different color signals for latch K10 of the R-G-B Output circuit. Lines DVY4-DVY7 carry data representing the Z-intensity signals for latch E6 of the Z Intensity and Blanking circuit. Data on DVY8-DVY10 are applied to latch D7 of the Vector Scal- Ing circuit. The data carried on these lines represents the number (in binary) that the Vector Scaling circuit uses to divide into the vector drawing time. The vector drawing time n Is divided by 2, where n equals the number represented on DVY8-DVY10. In addition, DVY11 and DVY12 are exclusive-ORed by gate B6 of the Normalization Flag circuit.

EAROMCON The Electrically-Alterable ROM Control signal is an active lowlevel signal software-generated by Address Decoder P3 at address 8900. ERROMCON is the clock signal for latch K2 In the High- Score Table circuit. EAROMCON allows K2 to pass data bits on lines DBO-DBS to the control lines of EAROM M2.

- 7000. EAROMRD Is the read-enable signa! for buffer H2 of the High-Score Table circuit. EAROMRD allows the eight data bits from EAROM M2 to be passed through buffer H2 to the microprocessor data bus.

1. Enter self-test and advance to diagonal crosshatch pattem (Screen 2).
